name: Fibrosarcoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Fibrosarcoma

criteria.description: Presence of malignant spindle-shaped fibroblastic cells arranged in a herringbone pattern on histology
Positive vimentin staining with absence of markers for other sarcomas (e.g., negative S-100, desmin, cytokeratin)
MRI or CT showing a soft tissue mass with heterogeneous enhancement and possible bone involvement
Presence of a progressively enlarging painless mass in soft tissue

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with characteristic spindle cell morphology and immunohistochemical profile; clinical and imaging findings supportive
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular genetic testing may assist in differential diagnosis but is not routinely required.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Painless progressively enlarging soft tissue mass

searchTerms: hard deep tumor felt under skin

common.symptomName: Localized swelling with limited range of motion if near joint
Occasional mild tenderness over tumor site
Soft tissue mass with irregular borders on imaging
searchTerms: soft tissue lump with uneven edges on scan

common.symptomName: Weight loss associated with advanced disease

occasional.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to nerve compression (e.g., paresthesia)
searchTerms: nerve pressure causing numbness or tingling

occasional.symptomName: Skin ulceration overlying tumor in advanced cases

searchTerms: fever due to tumor tissue death

occasional.symptomName: Pathological fracture if tumor invades bone
searchTerms: bone breaks caused by tumor invasion

rare.symptomName: Distant metastases presenting with respiratory symptoms

searchTerms: limb swelling due to blocked lymph vessels

laboratory: Elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in some cases
imaging: MRI showing heterogeneous soft tissue mass with infiltration
CT scan demonstrating soft tissue density with possible bone erosion
X-ray may show soft tissue swelling and bone involvement
other: Histopathology revealing spindle cells in herringbone pattern
Immunohistochemistry positive for vimentin, negative for S-100 and cytokeratin

distinguishingFeatures: Different immunohistochemical profile with CD68 positivity
Positive smooth muscle actin and desmin staining
More eosinophilic cytoplasm and cigar-shaped nuclei
Biphasic histology with epithelial and spindle cell components

redFlags: Neurological deficits due to nerve compression
references: Fletcher CDM, Bridge JA, Hogendoorn PCW, Mertens F. WHO Classification of Tumours of Soft Tissue and Bone. IARC; 2013.
Enzinger FM, Weiss SW. Soft Tissue Tumors. 5th ed. Mosby; 2008.
